claims.text: As-fabricated, pre-exposure Q235 steel contains inherent residual tensile stress.
As-fabricated Q235 steel contains elevated dislocation densities.
Residual tensile stresses in Q235 steel promote localized corrosion and pitting.
Dense dislocation structures create highly active micro-galvanic sites in Q235 steel.
The proposed micro-galvanic sites promote initiation and propagation of localized corrosion.
Low-temperature annealing can relieve residual stresses in Q235 steel.
Low-temperature annealing can relieve residual stress without significantly changing grain size or phase distribution.
Residual-stress relief produces a corresponding decrease in dislocation density at localized sites.
Localized stress and dislocation-rich sites typically serve as nucleation points for corrosion pits.
Elevated residual tensile stress and associated dislocation structures promote formation of micro-galvanic cells.
These micro-galvanic cells accelerate localized anodic dissolution and pit initiation.
Relieving residual stress reduces the driving force for micro-galvanic corrosion and suppresses corrosion onset.
Annealed Q235 specimens will have lower corrosion rates than untreated specimens in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature and 70°C.
Annealed Q235 specimens will have lower pit density than untreated specimens under the specified exposures.
Annealed specimens will display a more uniform corrosion morphology than untreated specimens.
The proposed mechanism applies to aggressive chloride environments from room temperature through 70°C.
Grain growth caused by annealing could independently influence corrosion behavior.
Annealing-induced phase transformation could independently influence corrosion behavior.

contradictions.description: The intervention says characterization should confirm that only residual stresses are modified, and the hypothesis says other microstructural features remain substantially unchanged, whereas the structural mediator explicitly predicts a decrease in dislocation density, itself a microstructural change.
